events.title: Ahasuerus Displays His Wealth at Susa
events.description: In the third year of his reign, Ahasuerus hosts officials, military leaders, and provincial nobles for an extended display of imperial wealth. He follows it with a seven-day banquet for Susa while Vashti separately entertains the women of the palace.

events.title: Vashti Is Removed as Queen
events.description: Vashti refuses the king's summons during the banquet. On his advisers' counsel, Ahasuerus bars her from his presence and circulates a decree throughout the empire concerning authority within each household.

events.title: Young Women Are Gathered for the King
events.description: The king's attendants organize a search for a new queen and gather young women into the royal harem. Esther, an orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, gains Hegai's favor while concealing her Jewish identity at Mordecai's direction.

events.title: Esther Is Crowned Queen
events.description: After the prescribed year of preparation, Esther is brought to Ahasuerus in the tenth month of his seventh year. The king chooses her as queen and celebrates with a banquet, provincial relief, and royal gifts.

events.title: Mordecai Uncovers an Assassination Plot
events.description: Mordecai learns that two royal eunuchs are plotting against Ahasuerus and reports the danger through Esther. The conspirators are executed after an investigation, and Mordecai's service is entered in the royal annals.

events.title: Haman Plots to Destroy the Jews
events.description: After his promotion, Haman becomes enraged when Mordecai refuses to honor him and resolves to destroy Mordecai's entire people. In the first month of Ahasuerus's twelfth year, lots designate the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, and Haman gains the king's authority for his plan.

events.title: The Destruction Edict Is Issued
events.description: Royal secretaries prepare Haman's decree in the languages of the empire, ordering the annihilation of the Jews and seizure of their goods on the appointed day. Couriers carry the sealed command from Susa, leaving the city in confusion.

events.title: Mordecai Appeals to Esther
events.description: Mordecai and Jewish communities mourn and fast after learning of the decree. Through Hathach, Mordecai urges Esther to plead for her people, and she resolves to approach the king after a three-day fast despite the danger.

events.title: Esther Approaches the King and Hosts a Banquet
events.description: On the third day Esther enters the inner court without a summons, and the king receives her favorably. She invites Ahasuerus and Haman to a banquet, then asks them to attend a second banquet where she will present her petition.

events.title: Haman Prepares a Gallows for Mordecai
events.description: Haman leaves Esther's banquet elated but is again enraged by Mordecai's refusal to honor him. At the urging of his wife and friends, he erects a high gallows and plans to seek Mordecai's execution before the next banquet.

events.title: Mordecai Receives Royal Honor
events.description: During a sleepless night, Ahasuerus hears from the annals that Mordecai's loyal service was never rewarded. Haman arrives seeking Mordecai's death but is instead ordered to robe him and lead him publicly through Susa in royal honor.

events.title: Esther Exposes Haman and Haman Is Executed
events.description: At her second banquet, Esther reveals her Jewish identity and identifies Haman as the author of the threat against her people. The enraged king orders Haman executed on the gallows prepared for Mordecai.

events.title: Mordecai Receives Haman's Authority
events.description: Ahasuerus gives Haman's estate to Esther, who discloses her relationship to Mordecai. The king transfers the royal signet ring to Mordecai, and Esther appoints him over Haman's property.

events.title: Mordecai Issues an Edict of Jewish Defense
events.description: Because the first royal decree cannot be revoked, Esther again petitions the king and receives authority for a countermeasure. Mordecai sends a sealed edict throughout the provinces permitting Jewish communities to assemble and defend themselves on the appointed day.

events.title: The New Edict Brings Joy
events.description: Mordecai leaves the king in royal attire as Susa celebrates. Across the empire, Jewish communities respond to the decree with feasting and honor, and many among the surrounding peoples identify themselves with the Jews.

events.title: The Jews Defend Themselves Across the Empire
events.description: On the day appointed by the decrees, Jewish communities assemble against those seeking their destruction and receive support from provincial officials influenced by Mordecai's power. They prevail throughout the provinces and in Susa but refrain from taking plunder.

events.title: The Defense Continues in Susa
events.description: At Esther's request, the king permits the Jews in Susa to assemble for a second day and orders Haman's ten sons displayed on the gallows. The Jews again defeat their enemies without taking plunder.

events.title: The Victories Are Celebrated
events.description: Jews in the provinces rest and feast on the fourteenth day, while those in Susa rest on the fifteenth after their additional day of defense. These differing celebrations shape the observance in villages and in Susa.

events.title: Mordecai and Esther Establish Purim
events.description: Mordecai writes to Jewish communities directing annual observance of the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the twelfth month with feasting, mutual gifts, and aid to the poor. Esther joins him in confirming the practice and its associated fasts in writing.

events.title: Mordecai Serves as Second to Ahasuerus
events.description: Mordecai rises to a rank second only to Ahasuerus. He uses his standing to seek the welfare of the Jewish people, and his prominence is recorded in the royal annals.
